jobs.title: Program Manager, Housing Place-Based Services
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Homebridge serves a high risk, high needs, complex-diagnosed population with a combination of domestic, personal, and paramedical homecare functions funded through IHSS. Our work allows an often-underserved population to live safely in their community. Homebridge offers a dynamic, fast-paced work environment with 350+ unionized field workers and 90+ internal office staff.

POSITION SUMMARY

Homebridge is seeking an experienced and mission-driven Program Manager to lead our MOHCD-funded Housing Place-Based Services program (Program Area 2). This role designs and oversees the quality of Homebridge's resident skills-building workshop model at four San Francisco properties, leads a team of trainers who are the primary deliverers of workshop content, facilitates selected sessions, manages day-to-day program coordination, and serves as Homebridge's primary liaison to MOHCD and to property management and lead service provider partners across all sites. The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management skills with experience navigating government grant compliance and building trust-based partnerships with affordable housing operators and service providers.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Program Design & Oversight

* Lead delivery at Windsor, Pacific Bay Inn, Minna Lee (DISH), and 1100 Ocean Avenue (Mercy Housing): four workshop series per property per year, 4–6 sessions each.
* Design and continuously refine the workshop curriculum framework across MOHCD's eligible content areas: Health & Wellness, Economic Mobility, Education, Life Skills, and Money Management.
* Ensure all programming is trauma-informed, culturally responsive, accessible, and additive to — not duplicative of — each site's existing on-site lead service provider programming.
* Establish and monitor performance targets aligned with MOHCD's Required Work Plan Table.

Trainer Team Leadership

* Lead, onboard, and coach a team of trainers who are the primary deliverers of workshop content.
* Assign trainers by site, topic, language, and schedule, and manage coverage.
* Provide ongoing training and support on trauma-informed practice, de-escalation, and culturally responsive facilitation.

Workshop Delivery & Program Coordination

* Facilitate selected workshop sessions directly, and cover sessions when needed.
* Manage day-to-day program coordination, including series calendars, room reservations, building logistics, and resident outreach and sign-ups with partner staff.
* Track attendance and outreach records, and manage incentives, refreshments, tablets, and workshop materials.

Partner & MOHCD Relations

* Serve as Homebridge's primary point of contact with MOHCD for this grant, including reporting, compliance, and site visits.
* Maintain relationships with property management and on-site lead service provider partners across all sites, including at least weekly coordination once services are operational.
* Lead partnership development for new sites, including securing Letters of Intent and Letters of Support.

Data, Evaluation & Compliance

* Oversee data collection, outcome tracking, and the annual client satisfaction survey process across all sites.
* Prepare and submit required MOHCD reports and deliverables.
* Ensure grant compliance with MOHCD requirements, including budget adherence and eligible use of funds.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

* Bachelor's degree in social work, public administration, public health, or a related field required; Master's degree preferred.
* 3+ years of experience in program management, ideally within affordable housing, homeless services, or community-based nonprofit settings.
* 2+ years of supervisory or team-lead experience, plus experience delivering adult workshops or training.
* Demonstrated experience managing government grants, including reporting, compliance, and budget oversight.
* Strong understanding of trauma-informed, culturally responsive service models.
* Excellent relationship-management skills with property managers, service provider partners, and government funders.
* Strong written communication skills, including grant reporting and narrative writing.
* Bilingual English/Spanish a plus.

Required Training and Certifications

* Trauma-informed care training completion required within first 90 days of hire (provided by Homebridge, or prior certification accepted).
* Mandated reporter training completion required.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

* Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Public Administration, Public Health, Human Services, Community Development, or a related field required;
  + Master's degree preferred.
* Minimum of 3–5 years of program management experience, preferably in affordable housing, homeless services, community-based organizations, or nonprofit settings.
* Minimum of 2 years of supervisory or team leadership experience, including staff development, coaching, and performance management.
* Demonstrated experience managing government-funded grants or contracts, including budget oversight, compliance, reporting, and deliverable management.
* Experience developing and facilitating community-based workshops or educational programming, building community partnerships, and working with diverse populations using trauma-informed and culturally responsive approaches.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is hybrid, combining office-based program management and MOHCD reporting work with regular travel across San Francisco partner properties for site visits and partner meetings. Some evening or weekend availability may be required for community events.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individual with disabilities to perform the essential functions. jobs.company: Community School of Music and Arts
jobs.title: Community Arts Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Community Arts Program Coordinator assists the Community Programs team in delivering high-quality programming to CSMA’s partners. Reporting to the Director of Community Programs, this role provides day-to-day administrative support for the Community Arts Programs, including: In-School Programs (Art4Schools, Music4Schools, After School), Artistic Intelligence, Mohr Gallery Community Artist Exhibitions and Events, and Community Events.

**Primary Duties and Responsibilities**

**In-School Programs**

* Coordinate with CSMA Community Program’s Team and school administrators about In-school program logistics (materials, scheduling, classroom roster, etc.).
* Collaborate with the Art4Schools (A4S) coordinator to ensure operations run smoothly for A4S Art shows, including tracking, picking up, and delivering all A4S art show materials.
* Collaborate with the Senior Coordinator to create Music4Schools kits for instructors and after-school class kits.
* Collaborate with the Program Team and Senior Coordinator to create two-three in school newsletters per year.
* Support off-site logistical arrangements such as delivering supplies to faculty, attending community partner events and engagement opportunities, i.e., resource fairs, M4S informances/concerts, A4S art shows, and family art nights.
* Support with creating draft flyers, templates, and supporting our team to get the word out into our community, i.e., flyer distribution at partner sites, local cafes, libraries, etc.

**Data Tracking and Scheduling**

* Collaborate with the Senior Program Coordinator to support the execution of accurate and easy-to-read faculty and school schedules.
* Support the Senior Program Coordinator with capturing and maintaining accurate partner data across spreadsheets, i.e In-School Key Data, Contact List, Program Key Dates, etc.

**Faculty & Substitute Teacher Support**

* Support Faculty with substitute teacher needs, i.e coordinating communication between faculty and school administration, gathering lesson plans, and providing all necessary assignment information for a successful day of teacher coverage.
* Create a substitute teacher teaching day(s) addendum that will support faculty with ADP input.
* Engage with faculty members regularly to guide them and to foster a long-term relationship with them.
* Utilize translation tools to translate Google Slides presentations to support In-School faculty with their ELL students.

**Onsite Support**

* Prepare the meeting space for the monthly Faculty meetings, including setting up hospitality, materials, and technology needed.
* Support and collaborate with the Senior Program Coordinator to oversee the Artistic Intelligence student worker program, volunteers, and interns.
* Support the Director of Community Programs with Mohr Gallery timeline tracking, installation, and deinstallation.

**Skills/Qualifications**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Arts Management, Business Administration, or related field (music or fine arts focus preferred) or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Experience: 1+ years of program or departmental administration preferred; recent graduates are encouraged to apply.
* Proactive team player, creative problem solver with a customer service mindset.
* Ability to communicate professionally, positively, and consistently with faculty, school administrators, teachers, and parents.
* Skilled at complex scheduling.
* Excellent organizational and administrative skills with careful attention to detail.
* Intermediate to expert ability to use Google Workspace.
* Familiarity with project management processes, concepts, and tools.
* Ability to travel to various teaching sites in the Bay Area, particularly Mountain View and Cupertino, but could include San Mateo, Redwood City, or San Jose occasionally.
* Love for music, art, and education required.

**Physical Demands**

* Occasionally required to sit; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl.
* Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
* Frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms.
* The employee must have reliable transportation to travel to all schools served by the in-school programs for meetings and other required tasks.

**Work Schedule**

* **1st 60 days:**

Hybrid: A minimum of three days on-site per week, with additional days as needed based on the program demands.

* **After 60 days of employment:**

Hybrid: A minimum of two days on-site per week, with additional days as needed based on the program demands.

* **Working hours:**

Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm

**About Community School of Music and Arts**

Founded in 1968, the Community School of Music and Arts is Northern California’s largest non-profit provider of arts education programs. With a $7 million budget and 160-member staff and faculty, CSMA is one of the ten largest community schools in the United States. Located in the heart of Silicon Valley, one of the global capitals of creativity, CSMA is dedicated to making the arts and arts education accessible to all, regardless of age, experience or background. Headquartered in the award-winning Finn Center in the City of Mountain View, CSMA directly serves over 30,000 people of all ages, skill levels and economic means each year, including over 21,000 students at 54 schools in San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties.

CSMA is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE AA M/F/Vet/Disability). Candidates from diverse backgrounds and bilingual candidates are encouraged to apply. CSMA is committed to creating an environment that embraces openness, respect, collaboration and accountability.

Pay: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour

Expected hours: 40.0 per week

* Employee assistance program
* Employee discount
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance

* Retirement plan

jobs.title: Care Coordinator: Interim Housing Program
jobs.description:
**About Cardea Health:**

Cardea Health is a non-profit organization dedicated to providing compassionate health care to marginalized populations.

**Misson Statement:**

Our mission is to create and support programs that protect the health and autonomy of vulnerable individuals and promote equity and social justice to improve the well-being of our entire community. Compassionate care for vulnerable populations.

**Workplace Culture:**

Cardea is dedicated to creating a workplace that celebrates diversity and actively seeks to include underrepresented communities. We believe that diversity drives innovation and fosters a more dynamic, inclusive, and productive work environment. We value unique perspectives, experiences, and talents, and we are committed to providing equitable opportunities for growth and advancement. Join us in building a team that reflects the rich diversity of our society and let's make a positive impact together.

Our Cardea CARE(S) Values include:

* Compassion
    
  Big heart, steady presence
* Accountability
    
  We own it: the work, the follow-through, the impact.
* Respect
    
  We assume good intent and keep it real
* Engagement
    
  We lean in and figure it out together.
* Support
    
  We’ve got each other across roles, teams, and sites.

These values guide how we care for residents, collaborate with colleagues, and represent Cardea Health in the community.

**Primary Work Location:** OTC

This position is based primarily at OakTown Collective a Cardea Health interim housing program serving individuals experiencing homelessness who may have complex medical, behavioral health, and social service needs.

Employees working at this location support residents in a housing-focused environment centered on stabilization, health, dignity, and connection to community resources and permanent housing opportunities.

Depending on the position, employees may regularly interact with residents, healthcare providers, case managers, housing navigators, community partners, visitors, and government agencies.

**Job Summary:**

The care coordinator will assist clinical staff and residents in the coordination of medical and behavioral health care.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Maintain a calendar of upcoming resident medical and behavioral health appointments. Communicate upcoming appointments to clients, clinical staff, and transportation services
* Assist clinical staff and site-based residents in the scheduling of client medical and behavioral health appointments.
    
  Communicate with local pharmacies regarding site-based resident prescriptions. At the direction of nursing staff request medication refills, deliveries, and transfers
* Request relevant medical records of site-based residents from hospitals and community clinics. Transmit medical records and other authorized requested documentation to partner clinics to facilitate care coordination
* Interface with site-based resident healthcare coverage plans to avoid interruption in services and facilitate care
* Take telephone messages and provide feedback and answers to patient/physician/pharmacy calls
* Ensure adherence to infection control standards on site among staff and residents
* Answer calls to the nursing station and respond independently to when appropriate
* Assist nursing staff with light clerical duties including filing and making copies
* Maintain confidentiality in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
* Practice harm reduction principles on site, including interventions that minimize harmful effects of substance use while treating all residents with dignity and respect
* Other duties as assigned
* Constant work around and/or with people OR Interaction with patients, clients, and external customers
* Clinical setting in a permanent supportive housing site

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* High School Diploma or equivalent
* Must be authorized to live and work in the U.S
* Must be at least 18 years of age
* Must have personal, reliable transportation to and from work sites and shifts

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Prior experience with homeless or incarcerated populations is desirable
* Self-directed and able to work with minimal supervision
* Detailed oriented and highly organized
* Must provide proof of COVID vaccination or willing to be vaccinated
* Prior experience with homeless or incarcerated populations is highly desirable
* Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel

**Physical Requirements:**

This position requires a combination of desk-based and active work activities.

Essential physical activities may include:

* Frequent sitting, standing, and walking.
* Movement throughout program sites, office locations, or community settings.
* Occasional stair climbing.
* Reaching, bending, kneeling, and crouching.
* Transporting supplies, equipment, files, or materials.
* Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull up to 25 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Work Environment:**

Cardea Health program locations operate within supportive housing, interim housing, medical respite, and community-based environments serving individuals experiencing homelessness and other vulnerable populations.

**Benefit:**

We offer access to competitive and comprehensive healthcare benefits such as: Medical, dental, vision, EAP, life insurance, long-term disability, HSA or FSA, Dependent Care FSA, voluntary benefits, paid sick leave, paid vacation time, birthday time off, and 401(k) with up to 3.5% employer match.

Benefit eligibility varies based on employment status, scheduled hours, and plan requirements. Full-time employees are generally eligible for employer-sponsored benefit contributions. Eligible part-time employees may participate in available benefit programs subject to plan terms. jobs.description:
We are so glad you are interested in joining Sutter Health!

**Organization:**

ABSMC-Ashby Campus

**Position Overview:**

Partners with Sutter Health patients in unique populations (oncology, bariatric, spinal trauma, stroke, etc.) and guides them through a comprehensive array of health services in accordance with established policies, procedures, protocols, techniques, and guidelines. Identifies and works to resolve barriers to care, assists with access issues, develops relationships with health care providers, explains insurance and payment systems, and coordinates services with providers, patients, and caregivers within Sutter Health, at external facilities, and in the community to provide seamless and integrated quality care. Raises awareness about healthcare organizations and agencies information resources, Sutter Health support programs and services, community resources, clinical trials, and helps to meet other illness-related needs identified by the patient, their family, or the patient's support group. Assists with ongoing evaluation and quality improvement of the program, including community outreach and marketing.

**Job Description**:

**EDUCATION:**  
*Equivalent experience will be accepted in lieu of the required degree or diploma.*  
  
Bachelor's: Social Work, Health Education or related field or equivalent education/experience  
  
**TYPICAL EXPERIENCE:**  
5 years of recent relevant experience.

**SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE:**  
In-depth knowledge of focus area, including diagnosis, current treatment options, complementary therapies, potential complications, family/support group dynamics and associate quality of life issues.  
  
Working knowledge of community resources for the assigned focus area, including requirements and accessibility.  
  
Thorough knowledge of healthcare systems, insurance/payment systems, and medical terminology.  
  
Solid analytical and project management skills, including the ability to analyze problems, reach practical conclusions, and institute effective changes.  
  
Possess written and verbal communications skills to explain clinical information and program data clearly and professionally to diverse audiences.  
  
Computer proficiency—Microsoft Office Suite, familiarity with databases, and experience with electronic health record systems.  
  
Work independently, as well as be part of a team, while demonstrating exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills.  
  
Prioritize and delegate assignments under varied and urgent conditions while working within standardized procedures and practices to achieve objectives and meet deadlines.  
  
Identify and solve complex problems based on the analysis of multiple sources of information while providing new perspectives on existing solutions.  
  
Ensure the privacy of each patient’s protected health information (phi).  
  
Build collaborative relationships with other healthcare providers (physicians, nurses, etc.), healthcare organizations and agencies, and community resources to coordinate efforts and provide the highest quality of patient care.

jobs.title: Office Manager / Receptionist (bilingual Spanish required)
jobs.description:
**Organization:** Compass Family Services is a 100+ year old nonprofit working on the front lines of San Francisco's homeless crisis. We provide families experiencing or at risk of homelessness with comprehensive support to address immediate needs and ensure long-term success.

**Program:** Holy Family Day Home offers a progressive, Reggio Emilia-inspired preschool curriculum which emphasizes individualized learning, self-exploration, play-oriented lessons, and child-initiated, teacher-led education. Daily activities include early literacy lessons, STEM learning, small classes in the art studio, and outdoor education in the community garden. These are all supported by our highly-qualified teaching staff and a wide variety of age-appropriate teaching tools.

**Schedule:** Monday – Friday, 37.5 hours per week. Daily schedule varies between 7:45 am – 5:00 pm based on Center needs.

**Location:** 299 Dolores St, San Francisco

**Organizational Core Competencies:** Accountable / Adaptable / Client-centered / Collaborative / Committed to diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging / Resourceful

**Responsibilities:**  
The primary duty of the Office Manager/Receptionist is to staff the front reception station of a large childcare center in the Mission District. The Office Manager/Receptionist is the first point of contact for families and other visitors. They greet families and children each morning, maintain the safety and security of our space, provide families with updates and resources, and provide administrative support to the management team. Specific job responsibilities include:

*Front Desk & Phone:*

* Greet all visitors as they enter the building.
* Answer calls and messages on the main phone line.
* Serve as the communication liaison between families and staff, relaying updates promptly and calling families to gather information as needed.
* Contact families about illness policies and when a child needs to be picked up due to illness or other emergencies.

*Attendance:*

* Support daily attendance, including morning/afternoon rosters, check-in, logging drop-off and pick-up times, and calling absent families.
* Maintain accurate attendance logs, and collect doctors' and parents' notes for monthly scanning and submission to the SFELA enrollment specialist.
* Track late drop-offs and late pick-ups against each family's contract hours.
* Verify authorized pick-up individuals, including ID checks and contacting families for authorization as needed.

*Records & Administration:*

* Enter data into CareConnect and other systems.
* Collect childcare fees.
* Assist teachers and administrative staff in collecting signatures from families on required documents in a timely manner.
* Provide clerical support, including sorting mail, contacting messenger services, copying, and filing.

*Facility:*

* Open the childcare center at 7:45 am and/or close center at 5:00 pm.
* Keep the lobby clean and well organized.
* Update and maintain bulletin boards with resources and information for families.
* Help stock office supplies as needed (e.g., paper, disinfectant).

**Qualifications:**

* **Fluent Spanish** **and** **English required**
* Demonstrated experience and ability to multi-task in a fast-paced front office environment
* One year of receptionist or similar customer service experience
* Experience in general office practices (filing, phones, typing, etc.).
* Computer literate including proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
* Good organizational skills
* Good communication and interpersonal skills, ability to work and communicate with children and families and the general public in a busy setting.
* Good judgement, calm demeanor, and discretion with regard to sensitive information.
* Ability to interact with families and children with patience and in a positive, friendly manner
* Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging work.

**Compensation and Benefits:**

* Salary: $30 - $33 per hour, 37.5 hours per week
* Paid time off: 4 weeks of vacation your first year, 5 in your second. Also paid holidays, sick time, family leave.
* Insurance: health, dental and vision insurance are fully covered by Compass for employees and dependent children. We also provide long term disability and life insurance.
* Retirement: after one year of work, Compass contributes an amount equal to 5% of your salary into a retirement account; this vests during years 2-6.
* Membership in OPEIU/Local 29 union

**To Apply:**

Please apply through our online application.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are an equal opportunity employer and actively seek to recruit a diverse workforce. Employees must embrace the idea that Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging contribute to the success of our underserved communities, and therefore to shared prosperity in our city and region. Compass Family Services is committed to the continuous work of implementing specific actions that will disrupt systemic prejudice and improve equity across programs and departments, to become an example to partners who also believe in a culture of inclusion that leverages diversity.

Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and California civil rights law, Compass Family Services will provide reasonable accommodation when requested by a qualified applicant or candidate with a disability, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship for the agency. Requests for reasonable accommodation apply to all aspects of the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please use the answer box for the final question of the job application to let us know.

jobs.title: Customer Support - Customer Support Associate
jobs.description:
At Veritext, we handle the details so legal professionals can focus on achieving outcomes.
  
  
**About the role:**  
Providing our clients with exceptional service is the foundation of our business. In Customer Support (Sales) you’ll play a crucial role in assisting our internal and external clients in all aspects of the sales process, including research, analysis and proposal and event support.
  
  
**What You'll Do:**  

* Utilize intermediate to advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP functions, and other formulas/calculations, to analyze sales data and support accurate reporting.
* Prepare, maintain, and validate sales reports and commission spreadsheets, ensuring data accuracy, consistency, and timely updates.
* Generate revenue reports to support market analysis, forecasting, and business insights.
* Research size and scope of respective clients to properly align revenue to internal organizational structure and effectively maximize client growth and retention.
* Review, assign, and verify commission allocations to ensure accurate revenue association for Account Executives.
* Perform training to external clients including but not limited to Zoom demonstrations, ES Client Demonstrations, Witness training and My Veritext Demonstrations.
* Provide support across various Sales related workflows and projects, continuously working to enhance job knowledge while bringing value to the organization.
* Act as a subject matter expert for using technology tools and sales reporting, i.e. Salesforce, Marketo and other resources as appropriate.
* Edit, update, and proof marketing materials for events, promotional campaigns, and client-facing flyers.
* Coordinate the ordering and distribution of branded marketing materials, including business cards, stickers, and promotional merchandise for client engagement.
* Manage registrations for Account Executives at client events, networking functions, and legal association memberships.
* Build and maintain positive relationships with our clients; surpass their expectations by anticipating their future needs.
* Maintain up-to-date knowledge of Veritext products, services, policies and best practices to provide a high level of support to clients, partners and internal sales team.

**What You Bring:**  

* 1+ year of related experience
* Salesforce experience preferred
* CRM experience preferred

jobs.title: Case Manager - HIV
jobs.description:
SUMMARY:

The Case Manager will provide comprehensive individualized case management services to people living with HIV (PLWH) in Alameda County. It is the responsibility of the HIV Case Manager to provide: a wide spectrum of services as a part of a primary care team; help to improve the health and well-being of our primary care patients and promote team functioning; and provide clinically and culturally sensitive outreach services to marginally housed adults in order to engage them in primary care services. Interventions may include crisis intervention, brief behavioral interventions, psychosocial assessments, collaboration with outside service providers, and appropriate internal/external referrals. Strong attention to detail as well as above-average interpersonal and organizational skills are necessary for the position. The position will require travel to sites throughout Alameda County.

This position reports to the HIV Program Manager.

This position is represented by SEIU-UHW. Salaries and benefits are set by a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), and an employee in this position must remain a member in good standing of SEIU-UHW, as defined in the CBA.

JOB DUTIES:

* Care coordination
* Primary Care coordination
* Help retain PLWH in care at the East Oakland Health Center. This includes reengaging patients who have had a lapse in medical care.
* Coordinates health care for individuals in need of assistance with adherence to medication. The goal is to help all PLWH to maintain an undetectable viral load. Assists with medication reconciliation.
* Links newly identified PLWH to available social services, including legal, housing, transportation, mental health, substance abuse, and pain management services.
* Tracks client follow up and care plan outcomes. Coordinates with medical providers regarding need for enhanced services.
* Documents client progress, referrals, encounters, services, and treatment progress in the centralized client management system to allow appropriate sharing with others program service providers.
* Assists with patients navigating barriers to care, treatment and social support:
* Assists patients in navigating the requirements of medical insurance.
* Enrolls patients in AIDS Drug Assistance Program.
* Eligibility determination to ensure access to community services.
* Tracks, manages, and facilitates specialty referrals to ensure patients are successfully linked to services.
* Makes appointments and completes reminder calls for primary care provider panel.
* Documentation
* Enters all encounters and units of service into the electronic medical record Epic, ARIES, and other data management systems as required.
* Maintains documentation of services to allow compliance with required reporting.
* Maintains strict adherence to all program requirements and deadlines including report deadlines and timely completeness of documentation for site visits and audits.
* Health coaching (patient self-management support)
* Coaches PLWH in self-management (e.g. medication adherence, lifestyle) including self-care skills.
* Assists patients in developing and executing health-related action plans or behavior changes based on client goals.
* Navigates problem-solving with patients as they encounter obstacles to achieving health-related goals.
* Conducts brief interventions with patients regarding alcohol and tobacco use and other behavioral health issues as appropriate.
* Agency and clinic meetings
* Participates in weekly case conferences with the HIV-Access team and monthly HIV Care and Prevention team meetings.
* Represents the HIV Access Program at regular meetings of the Alameda County Office of AIDS and the HIV Access division of the Community Health Consortium Network.
* Coordinates with other clinics within Lifelong Medical Care and across Alameda and Contra Costa Counties.
* Actively participates in clinic team meetings with internal staff and external partners.
* Other tasks
* Coordinate with the LifeLong Street Medicine teams to support PLWH who are homeless connect with the East Oakland Health Center or other LifeLong clinics, enroll in benefits, and connect to other social services.
* Contributes to clinic quality improvement planning and implementation.
* Coordinates operation of special projects as assigned by supervisor.
* Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

* Commitment to the provision of services for the underserved with demonstrated ability and sensitivity in working with a variety of people from low-income populations, with diverse educational, lifestyle, ethnic, and cultural origins.
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills with the ability to handle sensitive issues in a confidential, positive, and professional manner.
* Strong organizational, administrative, multi-tasking, prioritization, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to seek direction/approval on essential matters, yet work independently with little onsite supervision, using professional judgment and diplomacy.
* Work in a team-oriented environment with a number of professionals with different work styles and support needs.
* Conduct oneself in internal and external settings in a way that reflects positively on LifeLong Medical Care as an organization of professional, confident, and sensitive staff.
* Ability to see how one’s work intersects with that of other departments of LifeLong Medical Care and that of other partner organizations.
* Be creative and mature with a “can do,” proactive attitude and an ability to continuously “scan” the environment, identifying and taking advantage of opportunities for improvement.

Job Requirements:

* Prior experience in counseling patients, either in person or by phone.
* Proficient in MS Office/Excel.
* Strong customer service approach to problem solving and conflict resolution.
* Work/volunteer experience with and a commitment to serve people who are living with HIV/AIDS, people experiencing homelessness,

jobs.title: Program Manager - Youth Access Point
jobs.description:
**About us:** 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic is a community-based agency providing youth in the Bayview Hunters Point with medical and behavioral health services that encourage them to make decisions that support their health, safety, and development. 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic also manages a number of successful Transitional Age Youth (TAY) housing stabilization programs and one of the city’s few Youth Access Points.

**Program info:**The Youth Access Point (YAP) Program Manager oversees the operations of 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic's Youth Access Point and SFSU Rapid Rehousing (RRH) programs.

3rd Street operates one of San Francisco's Youth Access Points at our drop-in sites in Bayview and Hunters Point. The Youth Access Point serves as the frontline to San Francisco's Homelessness Response System, where transitional-age youth (ages 18–24) access Coordinated Entry services. These services include Problem Solving, housing assessments, referrals to emergency and long-term housing programs, and connections to supportive services designed to help young people achieve housing stability.

Our work takes place in a dynamic, high-intensity environment where participant needs, staffing demands, program priorities, and external requirements can shift quickly. The YAP Program Manager must be comfortable navigating complexity, responding to urgent situations, managing competing priorities, and leading a team through the realities of frontline service delivery.

The Youth Access Point Program Manager is responsible for the effective delivery, management, and continuous improvement of housing services for young adults. This position provides direct supervision and oversight of YAP and SFSU RRH staff and operations, including service planning and implementation, program and resource development, contract management, and personnel management, including hiring, coaching, training, and performance evaluation.

This is a highly hands-on management position that requires a balance of strategic leadership, program development, and day-to-day operational involvement. The Program Manager must be prepared to move fluidly between managing program operations, supporting staff through complex situations, responding to participant crises, addressing administrative and compliance demands, and ensuring program goals and deliverables are met.

The YAP and housing landscape is continually evolving, with frequent changes in local policies, funding priorities, eligibility requirements, service models, and system-wide expectations. The Program Manager must be comfortable operating in an environment where procedures and priorities may change frequently and where established processes are not always in place. This position will play an active role in developing new programs, building out service offerings, refining existing models, and translating emerging opportunities and requirements into effective program operations. The successful candidate must be comfortable building while simultaneously managing day-to-day operations.

The role requires a high degree of resilience, sound judgment, adaptability, and emotional intelligence. The successful candidate must be able to remain grounded and solution-oriented under pressure, navigate ambiguity, manage competing demands, and maintain accountability even when resources are limited or circumstances are challenging. This person must be willing to roll up their sleeves, step into operational gaps when necessary, and lead by example.

The Program Manager collects and analyzes outcomes data, prepares management reports, and leads significant program initiatives and improvement efforts. In partnership with the Assistant Director of Housing, the Program Manager represents the agency with funders, government agencies, and community providers. The position requires close collaboration with internal and external partners and may include direct service responsibilities such as case management, care coordination, crisis intervention, and mental health rehabilitation services.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

The following is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the Housing Program Manager. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned as needed.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

**Professional Development & Self-Leadership**

* Demonstrates emotional intelligence, self-awareness, and the ability to regulate emotions in high-pressure and emotionally demanding situations.
* Demonstrates resilience and adaptability when navigating organizational changes, staffing challenges, competing priorities, and unexpected operational demands.
* Maintains a solution-oriented approach when faced with challenges, ambiguity, and setbacks; takes initiative rather than waiting for direction.
* Demonstrates the ability to receive feedback, reflect on performance, acknowledge mistakes, and make necessary adjustments.
* Maintains healthy professional boundaries while demonstrating the flexibility and commitment required in frontline community-based work.
* Practices trauma-informed leadership, managing relationships, workload, and organizational change while maintaining personal well-being.
* Participates in supervision meetings, quality improvement activities, agency committees, peer reviews, and trainings.
* Demonstrates cultural responsiveness by working with the whole person in a welcoming, inclusive, respectful manner that embodies cultural humility.
* Seeks continuous professional development and uses performance evaluations and feedback for growth.

**Professional Ethics & Compliance**

* Maintains healthy interpersonal boundaries and adheres to all agency and industry ethical standards, including mandated reporting and participant confidentiality.
* Ensures compliance with all agency and program policies, including Boundary Code of Ethics, Core Competencies, Code of Conduct

jobs.description:
***Schedule: (Monday to Friday 8am-4:30pm)***

***Pay: $25.50-$38.50***

**ABOUT LIFEMOVES**

LifeMoves is the largest and most effective provider of housing and services for neighbors experiencing homelessness in Silicon Valley since 1987. Our Mission is to end homelessness by providing interim housing, supportive services, and building collaborative partnerships. With 40 programs, LifeMoves gives our neighbors experiencing homelessness a temporary place to call home while providing intensive, customized case management through site-based programs and community outreach.

**POSITION PURPOSE**

LifeMoves | First Step for Families (FSF) provides interim supportive housing in San Mateo to 39 families. During their stay, clients participate in holistic services tailored to each household’s unique needs and goals. Clients receive support to build self-sufficiency and return to housing stability, including but not limited to accommodations, meals, laundry, case management, and therapy. The team supports clients with housing, employment, benefits, physical and behavioral health through case management, workshops, and connection to specialized resources.

The First Step for Families Interim Supportive Housing (ISH) Case Manager (CM) reports to the site Program Director and provides case management, supports daily site operations, maintains a safe and welcoming environment, monitors the site, responds to client needs, and supports client check-ins, group activities, and overall site coordination. The position plays a key role in supporting people moving toward safe, stable housing and greater self-sufficiency. They provide case management services, life skills support, and resource connections and work in partnership with clients to set goals, celebrate progress, and overcome challenges. Using a trauma-informed and strengths-based approach, this position builds trust and respect, making sure clients feel heard, valued, and supported throughout their journey.

Key responsibilities include supporting clients by connecting them to services, building support networks, facilitating groups and activities, advocating for equitable access, and providing crisis intervention when needed. Beyond working directly with clients, this role may help to improve the overall program by sharing ideas, identifying service gaps, and helping strengthen community relationships. This role maintains clear documentation, contributes to program planning and reporting, and models professional, ethical behavior and works closely with their teammates to provide high-quality, coordinated care. Through their efforts, staff empower clients to grow their strengths, reach their goals, and build a better future.

**ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Client Support and Case Management**

* Develop and maintain individualized case plans focused on housing, employment, benefits, and overall well-being, based on each client’s strengths and goals.
* Support clients with housing searches, employment readiness, benefits enrollment (e.g., General Assistance, CalFresh, CAPI), and skill-building activities such as budgeting and daily living.
* Connect clients to healthcare providers and community resources, and assist with coordination, scheduling, and transportation as needed.
* Maintain accurate and timely client documentation and outcome tracking in HMIS and the agency’s client management system.
* Advocate for client needs and rights when working with partners, landlords, employers, or service agencies; provide mediation and conflict resolution support as needed.
* Provide calm, trauma-informed crisis response and ensure all client services align with ethical standards and agency values.

**Resource Connection and Community Collaboration**

* Build and maintain partnerships with community organizations, public agencies, and system partners (e.g., VA, APS, CPS, Probation) to support clients and improve access to resources.
* Serve as a liaison between LifeMoves and community stakeholders by sharing information, coordinating services, and promoting trauma-informed care practices.

**General Agency Responsibilities**

* Participate in weekly case conferences, monthly trainings, and regular supervision to strengthen skills.
* Fully participate in all required trainings. This includes completing trainings by assigned deadlines, actively engaging during sessions, and applying learnings to daily work.
* Attend continuing education opportunities to grow expertise and uphold agency standards.
* Be available to work occasional evenings and weekends as needed or as schedule describes.
* Perform other duties as assigned to meet program and organizational needs.

**Operations and Site Responsibilities**

* Support daily site operations, including inspections, maintenance coordination, donation management, and general facility upkeep.
* Assist with maintaining clean, safe, and organized living environments.
* Facilitate group sessions or workshops that promote skill development and confidence.

**SHIFT –** Monday-Friday 10:00am-6:30pm

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Educational Requirements:** Associate's Degree in related field preferred; or High School Diploma/GED with 2-5 years of equivalent experience in related field. Related fields may include direct involvement in peer advocacy, community outreach, housing services or roles within the homelessness services field.
* **Technology:** Comfortable using basic technology, including phone and messaging systems, email, Microsoft and Google Suites, and databases to complete administrative tasks and case management, reporting, and tracking outcomes.

Service Level Qualifications:

* **Care, Respect, Empathy:** Demonstrates empathy, professionalism, and respect for all individuals. **Emotional Regulation:** Stays calm and supportive in stressful situations and uses de-escalation skills. **Documentation:** Maintains clear documentation and organization. **Organization/Prioritization:** Organized, detail-oriented

jobs.title: Associate Project Manager (Quality Assurance & Improvement) Healthcare
jobs.description:
Overview:

Marin Community Clinics, founded in 1972, is today, a multi-clinic network with a wide array of integrated primary care, dental, behavioral, specialty and referral services. As a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), we provide vital health services to almost 40,000 individuals annually in Marin County. The Clinics regularly receive national awards from the Health Resources and Services Administrations (HRSA). Our Mission is to promote health and wellness through excellent, compassionate care for all.

The Quality Assurance & Improvement (“QA/I”) Associate Project Manager is responsible for working with the Director of QA/I to co-lead quality related performance monitoring, reporting and improvement efforts across all facets of the organization.

Responsibilities:

* Collaborate on the creation and execution of project work plans and revise as appropriate to meet changing needs and requirements.
* Using a data driven approach, work to identify opportunities for clinical, operational, and patient experience improvement, both organization-wide and individually by site.
* Collaborating with Quality team, contribute to design of improvement projects with goal of improving select key metrics.
* Track project plans and monitor progress in accomplishing project goals; identify key actions necessary to address problems/issues and with Director, contribute to recommendations to ensure projects are on track.
* With Director, work with clinical and operational leaders, as well as QA/I staff, to continuously develop, evaluate and improve specific QA/I approaches to key clinical and operational quality metrics.
* Strive to make QA/I metrics, goals and strategies familiar, meaningful and actionable across the organization and to promote a data-driven improvement culture by engaging staff in QI/A work.
* Develop and demonstrate knowledge of quality improvement theory and strategy, as well as expertise on key quality oversight programs and agencies relevant to FQHCs, including but not limited to Partnership Health Plan, DHCS, County of Marin, HRSA and NCQA.
* Serve as a QA/I liaison to a variety of healthcare clinical, operational, business and executive teams.
* In partnership with the Director of QA/I, support regularly scheduled improvement-focused meetings, including monthly site visits and Board Committee meetings, to review performance and outline QA/I strategies.
* Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Aptitude for conducting and interpreting complex quantitative/qualitative analyses.
* Skilled at leading, engaging, inspiring and supporting a team with a relational leadership approach.
* Excellent customer service skills.
* Strong analytical and/or operational problem-solving skills.
* Commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion in the workplace and knowledge or curiosity about fostering a trauma-informed work environment.
* Ability to receive and provide direction and collaborate with various positions and personnel levels within an organization.
* Discretion, confidentiality, tact, and ability to deal with sensitive issues.
* An interest and desire to advance the mission of Marin Community Clinics
* Bilingual English/Spanish is highly desirable, but not required.

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration or a related field required (in cases of an unrelated degree, at least two years of related analytical or quality improvement experience will be accepted in lieu of a Healthcare-related degree).
* At least one year of related analytical or quality improvement experience in a healthcare clinic setting.
* Exposure to complex project management required.
* Experience working in a Federally Qualified Health Center strongly desired.
* Expertise in SharePoint, Excel, Word,, and PowerPoint software programs or equivalents required.
* Experience with Epic desired, but not required.

**Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:**

* Fulfill immunization and fit for duty regulatory requirements.
* Prolonged standing and walking.
* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift to 15 pounds at times.
* Travel to clinic sites within assigned work area.

**Benefits:**

Our benefits program is designed to protect your health, family and way of life. We offer a competitive Benefits Program that includes affordable health insurance and Health Reimbursement Accounts (HRA), Dental and Vision Insurance, Educational and Continuing Education Benefits, Student Loan Repayment and Loan Forgiveness, Retirement Plan, Group Life and AD&D Insurance, Short term and Long Term Disability benefits, Professional Fee Reimbursement, Mileage and Cell Phone Reimbursement, Scrubs Reimbursement, Loupes Reimbursement, Employee Assistance Programs, Paid Holidays, Personal Days of Celebration, Paid time off, and Extended Illness Benefits.

Marin Community Clinics is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer.

Min: USD $40.78/Hr. Max: USD $47.86/Hr.

jobs.title: Case Manager II
jobs.description:
**JOB SUMMARY**: The Case Manager II (CM II), a key member of the primary care interdisciplinary team, provides services for patients with complex care needs. This position conducts patient outreach, engagement and psychosocial service assessment, assists in developing a patient-centered care plan, is the lead implementer of Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and coordinates service referrals and delivery. The Case Manager meets clients in home, clinic, or community as appropriate or required by the specific program/site. The CM II provides services to specific populations that have multiple complex health and social services needs and often provides care outside of a traditional health center setting, such as home visits, hospitals, supportive housing sites, encampments and shelters.

This position is represented by SEIU-UHW. Salaries and benefits are set by a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), and an employee in this position must remain a member in good standing of SEIU-UHW, as defined in the CBA.

**About us:**

As a Federally Qualified Health Center in Northern California with over 50 years of dedicated service to the community, LifeLong serves over 66,000 patients in the East Bay Area's socio-economically underserved regions. We provide medical, dental, behavioral health, and school-based services at more than 15 primary care sites across Oakland, Berkeley, and West Contra Costa County. From opening a residential respite program for homeless persons discharged from hospital to offering free testing to the community, we are innovative and responsive to our times' social and medical needs. We provide an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity and with which our patients can identify. To this end, we seek candidates who reflect the diversity of the East Bay communities we serve.

**Benefits:**

We offer excellent benefits: medical, dental, vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, dependent and domestic partner coverage, 403(b) retirement savings plan, and paid time off.

**Essential Functions**:

* Outreach, via telephone and in person at LifeLong, community and residential sites, to patients who meet case management program eligibility criteria or are prioritized by LifeLong for this service
* Proactively meet and engage with patients to build effective relationships and assess strengths and needs through use of standard intake, screening tools, and health, and social services records review
* Actively involve patients and caregivers, as appropriate, in designing and delivering services, including development of care plans, assuring alignment with patients’ values and expressed goals of care
* Provide and facilitate referrals for internal and external resources, and collaborate with the patient to complete required applications, forms, or releases of information
* Maintain a patient caseload in accordance with LifeLong standards for the specific population served or site requirements
* Utilize data registries and reports to manage caseload, meet program requirements, maintain grant deliverables, and promote high quality care
* Provide health education and training to patients, including but not limited to, harm reduction and disease risk-mitigation strategies that empower patients to manage their own health and wellness (e.g. overdose prevention, mitigating spread of communicable diseases)
* Assist patients with accessing and retaining public benefits and insurance (e.g. MediCal, SSI/SSDI, CalFresh, General Assistance, etc), and affordable/subsidized housing
* Respectfully and routinely communicate with patients, their care team members, external partners, and identified social supports
* Maintain knowledge of patients’ medical/behavioral health treatment plans and facilitate utilization of services by providing resources such as accompaniment, transportation, in-home care, reminder calls etc.
* Participate in team meetings to coordinate care, support patient goals, and reduce barriers to accessing services
* Advocate on behalf of patients to get their needs met and/or support patients to learn advocacy strategies for themselves.
* Provide case management services to patients with multiple complex acute or chronic medical or behavioral health conditions (e.g. HIV/AIDS, Hep C, congestive heart failure, severe diabetes, severe hypertension, psychosis, pregnancy, and homelessness)
* Provide general housing case management services that includes document readiness, housing problem solving, and assessments for Coordinated Entry System
* Assist with patient crisis intervention and de-escalation
* Provide and document billable services to eligible populations that result in revenue generation for LifeLong
* Keep current on community resources and social service supports to effectively serve the target population
* Document patient contacts/services in required data systems (EHR, HMIS etc.) according to LifeLong policy
* Specific activities may vary depending on the requirements of the program and funder.
* Promote diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in support of patients and staff
* Represent LifeLong positively in the community and advocate on behalf of underserved populations

**Qualifications**

* Commitment to working directly with low-income persons from diverse backgrounds in a culturally responsive manner
* Commitment to harm reduction, recovery, housing first, age-friendly and patient centered care
* Strong organizational, administrative and problem-solving skills, and ability to be flexible and adaptive to change while maintaining a positive attitude
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written skills
* Ability to prioritize tasks, work under pressure, and complete assignments in a timely manner
* Ability to seek direction/approval on essential matters, yet work independently, using professional judgment and diplomacy
* Works well in a team-oriented environment
* Conducts oneself in external settings in a way that reflects positively on your employer
* Ability

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
**Operations Manager – Retail**

**Job Overview**

We are seeking an organized and motivated Operations Manager to oversee daily retail store operations and support a positive customer and employee experience.

The ideal candidate will help coordinate store activities, supervise team performance, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure that operational procedures are followed efficiently. This role requires strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

The Operations Manager will work closely with store employees to maintain efficient workflows, support sales goals, and ensure customers receive professional and attentive service.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Supervise and support daily store operations and employee activities.
* Assist with recruitment, interviewing, onboarding, employee training, and professional development.
* Coordinate employee schedules, shift coverage, and timekeeping.
* Support payroll administration, bookkeeping, budgeting, and purchasing activities.
* Monitor inventory levels, stock replenishment, receiving, and inventory accuracy.
* Oversee merchandising, product displays, pricing, stocking, and overall store presentation.
* Ensure proper cash handling procedures and effective use of point-of-sale (POS) systems.
* Monitor sales performance and support the achievement of store sales objectives.
* Apply basic retail math and product knowledge to assist with operational and sales decisions.
* Respond to customer inquiries, resolve service concerns, and support a positive shopping experience.

* Strong leadership, team coordination, and organizational skills.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Good customer service and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to manage competing priorities and maintain effective time management.
* Familiarity with inventory management, purchasing, merchandising, and stock control.
* Knowledge of POS systems, cash handling, scheduling, and basic administrative procedures.
* Understanding of retail sales, pricing, budgeting, and basic bookkeeping.

This is an active retail management position that involves coordinating daily store activities, supporting employees, assisting customers, and maintaining efficient store operations.

jobs.title: Recruiting Operations Manager
jobs.description:
MongoDB is seeking a technical, execution-obsessed individual to join the Recruiting Operations team as a RecOps Partner. In this role, you will oversee RecTech and Process Optimization, serving as the primary strategic partner and operational liaison to HR Tech, translating Talent Acquisition strategy into an actionable systems roadmap. You will architect complex operational workflows, drive complex, multi-quarter roadmaps and bring the technical fluency and business acumen needed to evaluate the viability and impact of technical solutions.

Reporting directly to the Sr. Manager, CoreOps, you will operate with high autonomy to drive cross-functional execution and change management. You will provide strategic guidance, technical domain oversight, and peer mentorship to other individuals within the team, supporting them as individual product owners of their deliverables while elevating operational rigor across the team.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in New York City, Austin, Palo Alto, or San Francisco for our hybrid working model.

### **What You'll Do**

* Drive RecTech Modernization & Tooling Strategy: Act as the primary liaison to HR Tech to distill TA vision into a cohesive technology roadmap. Oversee high-complexity initiatives, such as the deployment of our Offer-to-Hire workflow using AI and automation and pilots for enterprise-grade interview and debrief intelligence suites
* Architect Complex Workflows & Systems: Develop end-to-end process maps for all key recruiting workflows to identify friction points and structural opportunities. Architect major workflow redesigns, such as overhauling the end-to-end offer process to minimize manual interventions
* Optimize Greenhouse as a Core System of Work: Consolidate high-priority issue areas across the hiring lifecycle to eliminate fragmented, manual workflows. Leverage native Greenhouse features and strategic integrations to standardize processes, lower compliance risks, eliminate administrative overhead, and elevate data integrity
* Drive Cross-Functional Execution & Autonomy: Independently own and drive goals, steering change management and adoption across global teams for all systems and process updates. Resolve complex escalations, operating with autonomy while proactively flagging for support when necessary
* Mentor Junior Members of the Team: Act as a dedicated mentor and sounding board for the RecTech and Process Optimization sub-domain owners, supporting their development into strong Product Owners without having direct administrative or people management duties
* Leverage Data to Drive Strategic Outcomes: Proactively identify internal TA needs (recruiters, coordinators, hiring teams), act as a compelling communicator across cross-functional groups, and regularly leverage data diagnostics to drive operational outcomes

### **What You'll Bring**

* Advanced Expertise: 8+ years of experience architecting complex operational workflows, recruiting technology evaluations and implementations, and multi-quarter systems roadmaps
* Scope & Complexity: Proven track record of independently owning multi-faceted goals, driving cross-functional execution, and resolving complex operational escalations. Operates with high autonomy and demonstrates sound judgment on when to flag for escalation
* Commitment to Mentorship & Influence: Proactively identifies TA needs, acts as a compelling communicator across technical and non-technical stakeholders, and demonstrates a proven ability to mentor and uplevel junior team members
* Technical Aptitude & Tooling Expertise: Deep technical knowledge of core recruiting platforms (e.g., Greenhouse, Gem, Guide). Proven track record of evaluating tool ROI systematically, sunsetting redundant platforms, and experimenting with automations and AI in recruiting workflows
* Workflow Architecture & People Team Alignment: Demonstrated experience redesigning complex hiring workflows and partnering with downstream teams (HRIS, HR Operations, FP&A) to ensure cross-system alignment and data hygiene
* Hands-On Data Fluency: Comfortability extracting and diagnosing pipeline and operational data directly in Google Sheets using advanced formulas to run ad-hoc analyses and diagnose root causes

### **About MongoDB**

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB's unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we're powering the next era of software.

Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It's what makes us MongoDB.

To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we're committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employees' wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Learn more about what it's like to work at MongoDB, and help us make an impact on the world!

MongoDB is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request an accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter.

jobs.description:

A career here is life-enhancing.

At Syner-G, we enable our people to build careers that impact positively on their quality of life. At Syner-G, we recognize that our team members are our most valuable asset. Join us in shaping the future, where your talents are valued, and your contributions make a meaningful impact.

For more information, visit www.Synergbiopharma.com

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**

Syner-G is seeking a Document Management Project Manager to support capital projects through effective document control, system administration, training, and user adoption activities. This role will serve as a subject matter resource for project documentation processes, document management systems, and Autodesk Forma, ensuring that project teams maintain accurate, compliant, and accessible project records throughout the project lifecycle.

The successful candidate will support capital project teams by managing documentation workflows, facilitating training sessions, leading onboarding activities, conducting Q&A support sessions, and driving adoption of document management best practices. This individual will collaborate with engineering, construction, facilities, and project stakeholders to ensure documentation standards are consistently applied across projects.

This position is internally classified as a Project Manager and will have a primary focus on project management.

**WORK LOCATION:**

Travel to client sites may be required based on project demands and training requirements.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

(This list is not exhaustive and may be supplemented or adjusted as necessary.)

* Serve as the primary resource for project document management processes and best practices.
* Manage and maintain capital project documentation throughout project planning, design, construction, commissioning, and closeout phases.
* Support document control activities, including document review workflows, version control, approval routing, retention, and archival processes.
* Administer and support Autodesk Forma and other project information management platforms.
* Develop, maintain, and improve document management procedures, standards, and work instructions.
* Facilitate onboarding sessions for new project team members and stakeholders utilizing document management systems.
* Deliver instructor-led and virtual training sessions related to document management processes, Autodesk Forma, and project documentation requirements.
* Conduct recurring Q&A sessions, office hours, and user support forums to address system and process questions.
* Provide first-level troubleshooting and user support for document management tools and workflows.
* Monitor document compliance and completeness throughout the project lifecycle.
* Coordinate with project managers, engineers, contractors, and external stakeholders to ensure required documentation is submitted, reviewed, and approved in accordance with project standards.
* Support data migration, document uploads, metadata management, and system organization activities.
* Generate document control reports, dashboards, and metrics to track adoption, compliance, and project documentation status.
* Assist with project turnover, ensuring complete and accurate documentation packages are delivered to operations and facilities teams.
* Maintain training materials, user guides, quick-reference documents, and standard operating procedures.
* Identify opportunities to improve document management workflows and enhance user experience.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements below represent the education, experience, skills, knowledge, and abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

*Education:*

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Information Management, Business, Education, or a related field preferred.
* Training, change management, or document control certifications are a plus.

*Technical Experience:*

* 3-7+ years of experience in document management, document control, project coordination, project support, or related roles.
* Experience supporting Capital Expenditure (CapEx) projects and associated documentation requirements.
* Experience administering or supporting Autodesk Forma strongly preferred.
* Experience working with document management systems, project collaboration platforms, or Common Data Env

jobs.description:

--------------------

The Design Project Manager is responsible for managing the preconstruction process for design-build and design-assist projects. This role leads project design and detailing activities, coordinates multidisciplinary teams, manages project schedules and budgets, and supports successful project delivery from concept through construction. The Design Project Manager serves as a key liaison between engineering, operations, estimating, business development, and clients while ensuring projects meet quality, budget, and schedule expectations.

* Manage large or multiple concurrent design-build and design-assist projects.
* Ensure projects are delivered on schedule, within budget, and to quality standards.
* Develop and maintain positive client relationships throughout project execution.
* Coordinate activities with architects, consultants, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams.
* Communicate project objectives, schedules, budgets, and risks across engineering, estimating, business development, and construction teams.
* Identify project risks and support mitigation planning throughout all project phases.
* Manage financial performance of design contracts, including costs, billings, collections, profitability, and cash flow.

* Coordinate engineering resources to support conceptual design development and estimating activities.

* Act as the single accountable owner, main point of contact, and critical issue path for assigned products, and communicate the product roadmap to partners and internal Micron customers.
* Lead the matrixed team (design engineering, supply chain, quality, test, and CM partners) and engage the right Domain Experts (SMEs) to resolve technical issues and support program execution.

* 8+ years in the semiconductor or electronics manufacturing industry, ideally with semiconductor test or burn-in hardware.

**Systems and Tools**

Microsoft Project or similar scheduling software; PLM and document control systems (for example Siemens Teamcenter); ERP systems (for example SAP); Tracking tools such as Jira or Smartsheet; and Microsoft 365, including Advanced Excel, Power Point, Teams, and SharePoint. Power BI or Tableau experience.

jobs.title: Program Lead, Global Rider Experience
jobs.description:
About the Team  
  
The Global Rider team in Community Operations (CommOps) owns the end-to-end support experience for Uber Mobility riders worldwide. Our mission is simple: **fix the upstream causes of rider defects in the product before support is needed, and make resolution fast, fair and seamless when a defect does occur.** Our North Star is the **Rider Defect Rate.**  
  
In 2027, our core focus will be to:  

* Eliminate rider defects, in particular charge riders transparently and accurately for their experience
* Make live chat the default modality following GenAI to enable fast resolution for all customer
* Create clear, trusted outcomes and match customer value and needs to the right level of support

  
About the Role  
  
You will report to the Global Rider Persona Lead. Most team members own a policy area end to end such as cancellations, fare disputes, driver feedback or lost item. **This role is different: you will own a portfolio of transversal programs that cut across those policies.** These are problems no single policy owner can solve alone, and solving them consistently across policies has an outsized effect on rider trust, resolution quality and cost.  
  
You will work with Tech (Customer Obsession and core product teams),CommOps functional teams (GDX, GSO, Central CommOps, PIR, Risk, Finance, CRM, Content, L&D) and regional CommOps POCs to turn several separate policy initiatives into one coherent global program each.  
  
What You'll Do  

* **Lead a portfolio of transversal programs** that cut across rider policies: define the scope, success metrics, governance and roadmap of each, and agree clear decision rights with policy owners, Product and Ops partners. The portfolio is expected to evolve, with new cross-policy topics added as opportunities emerge. Initiatives could include for example:
  + **GenAI resolution (Lumen and Nova):** driving cross-policy improvements to AI-led resolution, for example raising CSAT on Nova FAQ answers, improving intent accuracy and making sure riders are routed to the right resolution path.
  + **Agent enablement in a post-automation world:** shaping how human agents are equipped where automation stops, including: agent tooling, the right agent profile and KPIs (in particular on quality) with our BPO partners.
  + **Driver behavior and top defect creators (Driver Induced Rider Support):** bringing together education, feedback and proactive decisioning efforts aimed at the small group of drivers who generate a large share of defects
  + **Refunds, appeasements and goodwill frameworks:** building a consistent way to recover the rider experience across policies, and monitoring and optimizing spend with Finance and Risk.
* **Find key experience gaps** across policies, along with emerging trends and drivers of customer satisfaction, and use them to shape strategy and roadmap decisions.
* **Own tracking, reporting and performance insights** for your programs (defect rate, resolution rate, iCSAT, spend, agent KPIs) so that prioritization is driven by data.
* **Build the customer intelligence engine** for transversal topics: turn contact signals, sentiment and defect data into sized, prioritized cases that upstream product and ops teams act on.
* **Manage stakeholder alignment** across engineering, data science, product, regional operations, Risk, Finance and other support teams to unblock dependencies and protect execution quality.
* **Partner with the Global Driver team** to keep things fair on both sides and assess how changes affect drivers.

  
Basic Qualifications  

* Minimum 5 years of professional experience in customer experience operations, product operations, strategy or program management at tech or marketplace scale.
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in business administration, finance, engineering or a related field.
* Proven experience leading cross-functional programs that span several teams, policies or business lines without direct authority.

  
Preferred Qualifications  

* 8+ years of professional experience in customer experience operations, product operations, strategy or program management at tech or marketplace scale.
* Track record of managing and scaling product-adjacent customer lifecycles, billing or refund operations, or digital/AI resolution workflows.
* Experience designing financial guardrails or compensation and recovery frameworks (refunds, credits, goodwill) that balance customer experience with cost.
* Experience with AI-led customer support, agent operations, workforce or BPO management, or knowledge-base and content strategy.
* Strong skill in using large volumes of customer data, statistical tracking and operational KPIs to influence engineering and business roadmaps.
* Exceptional structured thinking: able to spot common patterns across seemingly separate problems and turn them into scalable frameworks.
* Adaptability and resilience in a matrixed, fast-changing organization, and comfort executing under tight deadlines.

  
For New York City, NY-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $162,000 per year - USD $180,000 per year.  
  
For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $162,000 per year - USD $180,000 per year.
